Career cell note, 3 October. Written by Uma, peer-earning mentor.
In early September Varun told me he was doing three things at once: tutoring two Class 10 students, freelance slide design, and online data entry for a small firm. He wasn't sure which was worth it. I suggested he log hours and payments for a month.
Today he brought the log. Tutoring: 16 hours, ₹4,800. Slides: 10 hours, ₹2,500. Data entry: 20 hours, ₹2,000. He worked out the hourly figures on my whiteboard: ₹300, ₹250, ₹100. He stood looking at the last one. 'It felt safe because it was always there,' he said. 'But it's nearly half my hours for about a fifth of the money.'
He decided to finish this week's data entry and then stop, and use those evenings for one more tutoring slot. I will ask him in November how the change is going.

qa.q: How many hours did Varun spend on data entry that month?
What does Varun's remark 'It felt safe because it was always there' reveal?
qa.a: He had felt secure with the steady data entry, and seeing ₹100 an hour leaves him surprised and a little deflated before he decides.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Varun after this month?
qa.a: Dropping data entry first makes sense; he could also keep logging another month to check that the tutoring and slide figures hold steady.

qa.q: How does the change look to the mentor who wrote the note?
qa.a: The mentor sees the log doing its job: Varun reached the decision from his own numbers, and a November check-in is planned.

grounding: Shows a student comparing a month of hourly earnings across three kinds of work and dropping data entry as the weakest.

Sunday, 30 June
Kiran's month-end accounts, done at last on the hostel bed. Hansa made me do it properly, with a table.
Tutoring, Class 7 science, Mon/Wed/Fri: 12 hours, ₹3,000.
Captions for a local news channel's clips: 9 hours, ₹1,800.
Data entry from home: 18 hours, ₹1,440.
I kept dividing because I didn't believe it. ₹250 an hour, ₹200 an hour, ₹80 an hour. The data entry is what eats most of my nights, eyes burning, earphones in so I don't fall asleep.
Hansa just said, 'So?'
So. I emailed the agency tonight to say July is my last month. Weird feeling. It was the first job I ever got, and I was proud of it. But I'd rather spend those eighteen hours on two more tuition kids, or on sleep.

qa.q: How many hours did Kiran spend on data entry?
What mixed feelings does Kiran have about dropping data entry?
qa.a: Kiran feels strange and a little sad letting go of a first job that brought pride, but relieved to free those hours.

qa.q: What else could Kiran check before the next month's table?
qa.a: Kiran could add travel and preparation time for tutoring, to be sure the ₹250 figure really holds.

qa.q: How might Hansa see Kiran's decision?
qa.a: Hansa probably sees it as the obvious result of the table, which is why the only reply is 'So?'

grounding: Shows a student comparing a month's hourly earnings for tutoring, freelance captions and data entry, and dropping data entry.
